utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good morning to you, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, I would like to remind that you the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony still binds you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, are you -- oh no, before we start, there was a deadline set on last Monday concerning translations. We have received a submission by the Cermak Defence, not by any of the other Defence teems, neither by the Prosecution. Should the Chamber understand that there's nothing to report? If you'd like to take your time until after the first break and verify, then of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could just chat about it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll then hear from the parties other than the Cermak Defence after the first break. Ms. Higgins, are you ready to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, from my recollection, I think we were dealing with or about to deal with P500.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: So if that could be brought up on to the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Berikoff, just to explain this for you, we have in front of us here Prosecution document. It's a Prosecution organigram showing the hierarchy of the Croatian civilian police and the lines of subordination from, you see at the very top, the ministry level?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And it goes all the way down to the bottom to the police stations on the ground.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: It's fair to say that you, as we established yesterday, we were not familiar with the names on the chart?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I will really try today. Sorry, apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just take a moment, Mr. Berikoff, please, to just cast your eye over the names on that chart. It's right, isn't it, that from the top to the bottom, concerning control and command, that is illustrated in that chart, there is no mention of the name Juric. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And there is no mention of the name Cermak. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, you haven't had the opportunity of seeing this before, have you?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And we know that post Operation Storm, if we calculate it from that time, you were only in the region for four weeks, in fact, approximately?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Right to say that you weren't familiar with the complexities of the structure in Croatia as regards to the Ministry of Interior and the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: To use your words, and to put this into a context, given the limited time you were there, you made assumptions about the way things worked in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in all of Croatia, ma`am. However, in the area that I was operating in, the answer to that is yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you. I accept that. Thank you. Now, given that I have limited time this morning, what I'd like to do is make one point clear and deal with an example. Going back to your diagram now, please, which is P745.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If that could be put up onto the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I think I made it very clear yesterday that there isn't one point of this diagram that is accepted by the Defence but what I'd like to do, Mr. Berikoff, is take an example. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And the example I'd like to take is the name that appears on that chart. Let's take the individual you've named, Major Juric. Now, you told me yesterday that you didn't know who appointed Mr. Juric. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Have you heard the name Mate Lausic, the chief of police administration?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Had you heard about the 72nd and the 73rd Military Police battalions operating in Sector South?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Is it right that you haven't been shown any military police documents by the Prosecution, to support this notion of subordination of Juric to Cermak?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That statement is correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, if I could, please, have on the screen D267, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: To put this into context for you, Mr. Berikoff, I'm going to take you through the document. I'm presuming that you have never seen this document or been shown it by the Prosecution on the front page, as you see it?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen this document, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: It's a document dated, as you can see, the 2nd of August, and you will see, as we go through it, that it is from Major-General Mate Lausic and you can see the addressees there on the right-hand side of the page. Can you see those?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And you will note that the garrison is nowhere to be seen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, if I could move, please, to page 4 of that document, four of six. Sorry, just to make the point clearly I should have been more precise and said the Knin garrison was not on that front sheet.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood what you meant, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Berikoff. Paragraph 10, if you look at the second part of that, the second paragraph of paragraph 10, you can see there from this contemporaneous document and I will take you to the end so you can see Mate Lausic's name: I appoint major Ivan Juric, and if you look through you can see that it refers to him assisting in commanding and organizing the activities of the 72nd Military Police Battalion and the 73rd Split Military Police Battalion and that the commanders of those two battalions shall be subordinated to Major Ivan Juric. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If I could follow through by taking you to the next page of that document, please. Because one point that we have looked at is the context of reporting, so it may be important to establish who, in fact, Mr. Juric was supposed to be reporting to. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: If we look on this page, the paragraph that begins: "Every day at 2000 hours," and you just read that through to yourself, Mr. Berikoff. To put it in a nutshell, the commanders of the 72nd and the 73rd were to report to Mr. -- Major Ivan Juric who shall then report to the military police administration, the chief of which was Major-General Mate Lausic. Do you see that context?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: One more document, I'd like, please, on the screen -- sorry, before I leave that. Again, if you look at the bottom of that screen you'll note again the delivered to, there is no mention of the Knin garrison. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is it correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Could I have please have on the screen D268.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just while it is coming on to the screen, this is a document dated the 2nd August 1995. It's, again a document from Major-General Mate Lausic to various units of the military police administration. You can see the front page there and the addressees, VP, General police, UVP? Can you see that at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like, please, to turn to page 3 of that document. This document illustrates the expansion of Mate -- sorry, of Juric's tasks and you can see there in that second paragraph it refers to the cooperation and coordination and who he was to do that with. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And if you look through the names, again, the Knin garrison is not a name that we find there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, Your Honour, there are four other documents in a series which show the reporting that continues between Mate Lausic and Juric on the 9th, the 10th, the 11th and the 12th of August. I don't intend to take this witness through them but I've discussed it with my learned friend, Mr. Russo there are 65 ter documents and he accepts that they can be admitted into evidence and I would seek their admission before the Chamber. I can give the document references to put this question into a context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, even without asking you, I take it that Ms. Higgins has informed the Chamber accurately on your consent, so if I do not hear from you, that's how I always expect the parties to behave. Then, could you please give the 65 ter numbers, and we have seen now two documents --

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- so they need a number to be assigned to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: They're already D exhibits, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh yes, yes, I remember that you referred to them as D exhibits. Then the 65 ter numbers of the other documents are.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: The first document is 3225, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D732.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next one, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D733, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the last one, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: The next one is 543, 65 ter.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit number D734, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And, in fact, Your Honour is right, because the last document I would seek to tender is in fact D211, just for the Chamber's note. That forms the last document in that series. So there is no need for another number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D732, D733, and D734 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: From the contemporaneous documents that have been shown to you this morning, Mr. Berikoff, you would agree with me, I presume that there is no evidence there to show a line of subordination or control and command between Major Juric and Ivan Cermak. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, I was not privy to any of these documents that you have shown me this morning. However, I would agree to the contents of them but on the ground what I saw was a different situation at the time, in my own personal assessment. But the documents, I had not seen them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins, the witness has not had an opportunity to fully check that, but of course you would not have asked that question if there was any link in there and the Chamber of course itself can check the content of the documents and see whether the Chamber doesn't find anything in there, but especially since three documents have not even been shown to the witness, he couldn't expound on that --

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but from what he has seen he agrees with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Yes, I take that point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That documentation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just dealing with one brief reference that you made there, Mr. Berikoff, please take it from me, I'm only trying to show you information that I know you weren't privy to at the time but you see why I'm doing what I'm doing?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand exactly what you're doing, ma`am. No problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And the other point is this. That you said that in your last response: What I saw was a different situation on the ground in my personal assessment.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Just to remind you of yesterday, you did agree, however, that you had never seen or heard an order given by Mr. Cermak to Major Juric. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And it's right that you are not able - and I wouldn't expect you to be able - to produce any documents to show a contrary picture in terms of the documentation, Mr. Berikoff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to pull back up on to the screen your diagram. I think we're all very familiar it by now and I know you have a copy in front of you. But just to deal very briefly with your reference there to the 7th Guards Brigade and the 3rd Guards Brigade, just to -- so I'm clear, Mr. Berikoff, you have no documents to support that. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, ma`am. It's just what I saw on the ground of when the 7th came in and that the 3rd replaced.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: That is it very different, isn't it, from saying that they were --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: -- subordinated to Mr. Cermak ?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: So my point is no document to show that line of subordination, correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, no, I don't, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Neither, Mr. Berikoff, have you been shown any document since you made your first statement in 1996 to support that by the Prosecution. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Did you know or were you ever informed of the fact of a military structure operating in Sector South completely outside the role and function of General Cermak as garrison commander?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Now, considering yesterday's evidence and today, and you understand that I understand your limited time in that area, considering that, could it perhaps be that you have made a rash judgement about the actual true role and capabilities of Mr. Cermak, Mr. Berikoff?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I can't answer that question, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as an information officer, did you know that in the early days of the formation of the Croatian state even leading political figures were given military ranks, regardless of their military function and experience? Did you come to know about that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Let me just finish by asking you this, Mr. Berikoff. Would this be fair and accurate to say that the indicators of authority that you relied on in relation to Mr. Cermak boiled down to the following. Firstly, he wore a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Secondly, you knew he had a rank.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And those were two factors you relied on?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were two of the factors, yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: There was also the letter which we discussed which, to be fair, you had described as a joke. But there was the letter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And there was the title which you have now seen from contemporaneous documents was incorrect. Yes?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And it amounts -- that would be a fair summary. Would that be right, Mr. Berikoff?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be a fair summary, ma`am. However, you have to take into consideration that General Forand dealt constantly with General Cermak, Colonel Tymchuk dealt with General Cermak I believe, so it was the people involved with their dealings with General Cermak that also led me to my assessment, ma`am?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And this Court has heard evidence from General Forand and obviously what we're interested in is the basis and remit of your knowledge. You understand?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: And we discussed that remit yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, have you heard of the phrase don't shoot the messenger?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you very much, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, ma`am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, you're on your feet, and in light of what we heard last week, I take it that you'll cross-examine Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic who is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Berikoff.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to follow up along the lines with Ms. Higgins with respect to exhibits D267 and D268 as well as the newly marked exhibits that you had not seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's put up first D267, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And while that is coming up, Mr. Berikoff, your job was that of an intelligence information officer in Sector South. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And is it fair to state that people were relying upon you for information upon which to describe the situation on the ground or to make assessments on things that have happened during -- before and during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the extent that I was able to get that information, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And would you agree with me if that information was incorrect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, for you, pauses as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Berikoff, to the extent that you could assist Mr. Kuzmanovic in creating the quiet atmosphere for interpreters and transcribers, it would be highly appreciated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I lost myself there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, I think I'm looking back at the transcript so I can repeat my question. It is fair to state that the people, your superiors in many instances who were relying upon you for information, if the information was wrong that information ended up getting spread to the outside world. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In the early stages I was one of the few people that was able to get -- make my way throughout the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Nonetheless, if the information that you had received about, for example, certain units and certain locations was incorrect then that information would get spread not just to members of Sector South but to the media and to the outside world. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite possible. I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 267, which is up on the screen, is a military police document and if we can go on the first page, you see that nowhere in this particular document is the Ministry of Interior special police mentioned in any shape or form. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever seen any documents provided to you by the Office of the Prosecutor that describe the role, the location, the outfitting and the function of the Ministry of Interior special police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we go to the last page of this document, please. Why don't we go to the second-last page where it shows the cc's, to whom the document was copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we see to whom the document was delivered, there is no notation of any Ministry of Interior special police, either commander or officer, or member that received a copy -- or that was delivered a copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And without going through all of the other documents, I -- I presume, Mr. Russo would agree with me that D268, as well as D732, D733, D734, and D211, none of those documents indicate any copying in or reference to the Ministry of Interior special police that you're aware of, Mr. Berikoff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen the documents, so therefore, I would have to yes, I agree with you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the diagram that you were shown -- or that you drew which was P745 that we've seen -- and for your benefit I'd ask that it be put back up on the screen, so if you want to refer to it, you can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, in view of the authorities to which -- to which this letter was cc'ed I must admit that I do not have on my mind all the abbreviations we find in that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask, Your Honour, if it is all right to -- and I did not have a chance to speak with Mr. Russo about this the way Ms. Higgins did but I mean if he would agree that known of those documents refer to or have anything to do with the Ministry of Interior special police then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would have no problems. Perhaps if you, together with Mr. Russo, could prepare just a short list of what UVP exactly meant, et cetera I don't have it on my mind at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it's not only what it doesn't mean, but also --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What it does mean, understood, Your Honour. VP means military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the few that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... police, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. We've got your diagram up, Mr. Berikoff. This is a diagram that you put together. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. When did you put that together?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was during the interview with Mr. Elfgren during one of the interviews, and it was done quickly as Ms. Higgins had suggested. Basically like on a scrap of paper, to the best of my recollection, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And you have seen at least two of the documents now D267 and D268, where you have Major Ivan Juric, special police. Can you explain to me, please, what facts led you to believe that Major Ivan Juric had anything to do with the special police? I'm just liking for facts.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the factors I took into consideration when I placed Major Ivan Juric was part of the special police was the fact that he was wearing grey coveralls. Now, this may seem silly on the surface. However, I was informed by headquarters in Zagreb that members of the special police wore grey coveralls. I don't recall who told me, but it was through the intelligence section in headquarters UNCRO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So the sole basis for you to come to the conclusion that Major Ivan Juric had anything to do with the special police had to do with grey coveralls?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: As silly as it sounds, that's correct, sir, because people in grey coveralls responded to him and he also wore them as well, and from the information I received from Zagreb, yes, that is what I base my assessment on, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And was your basis that these were special police who were from the Ministry of Interior special police or some other kind of special police or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So fair to state that the only basis for you to conclude that Major Ivan Juric had anything to do what you term to be special police were grey coveralls?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that was something that was told to you verbally by HQ in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: As an information intelligence officer did you attempt in any way to find out from the Croatian authorities what the hierarchy or structure was of the Ministry of Interior special police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained yesterday, I'd just been in country a short time and didn't have an opportunity yet to do that. Had I stayed on, that would have been part of my duty, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that during the course of Operation Storm and the aftermath of Operation Storm it would be fairly important to accurately identify who you saw conducting activities on the ground?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to agree with you. However, at the time I was travelling throughout the sector to try and get as much raw information as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could it have been something as simple as calling the -- either the Ministry of Interior or the Chief of Staff of the Croatian military through your office in Zagreb to determine what units were where and what they were wearing and what kind of weapons they were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly pause between question and answer again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In response to that question, sir, I had informed Zagreb, both at the Canadian intelligence cell, the G2 cell, as well as the intelligence cell in UNCRO headquarters of my findings. It was not my responsibility to contact the Croatians with regard to the Ministry of Defence. That was at a higher level than myself, sir. I would have expected the headquarters in Zagreb to have done that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor ever tell you that your identification of these units in various areas, such as Cetina, Civljane, Kistanje, and other places were not in fact Ministry of Interior special police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never told anything by the OTP regarding this, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the person that you spoke with at G2 intelligence who told you the grey coverall ID in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall, sir. That's 13 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, and I apologise to the interpreters for my speed. I will do my best to calm down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. ... Mr. Kuzmanovic, if I give a sign to calm down, if you start apologising, then that has to be translated as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm looking at the witness, and it is difficult for me to see and I will -- you, so I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Berikoff, you gave several statements to the Office of the Prosecutor in this case, the most recent statement being 30 August 2008? And if we could go into closed session just for a moment, Your Honour. Or private session, I'm sorry. Relating to this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please have 3D00-001868 and not to be shown to the public, please. Not there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's supposed to be up, but I don't know why it isn't. Oh, here we go. All right. Thank you. If we could go to page 2 of that document, please. Fifth paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, the paragraph that I'm referring to for my next series of questions starts with: "Mr. Berikoff stated that his understanding of the 'special police' was that they were part of the HV and that they sometimes wore grey coverall-style uniforms." Now, you said that the sole reason that you came to that conclusion was a verbal that you got from someone at G2 in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your understanding was that the special police of the Ministry of the Interior was attached to the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I was not aware that the special police were part of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So at least as of -- when did you come to the conclusion that the special police were not a part of the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably came to that -- or I did come to that conclusion when I was dealing with other cases while I worked in the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So essentially until 2008, as of -- that correction was not made in your supplemental information sheet dated 30 August 2008. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you become aware that the special police of the Ministry of Interior was not a part of the Croatian military? What year?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never studied the Croatian forces in detail, so even to, right now, I cannot answer that question probably accurately. My assessments are from dealing with both the Bosnian side and the Serb side. I had no -- no dealings once I came to the OTP with the Croatian organisation chart, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you agree with me, Mr. Berikoff, that as a military intelligence information officer that it would be rather important and, particularly when it comes to a criminal matter, crucial to know who was subordinated to whom and what the order of battle was?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be, sir, but once I came to the OTP I was basically requested to stay totally away from any of the Croatian cases, which I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And I understand that, Mr. Berikoff, but you didn't even change your knowledge of the background and structure of the special police of the Ministry of Interior in your 30 August 2008 supplemental information sheet?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I didn't, sir, based on the -- or my reasoning being that this was information at that time, not what I had learned after working in the OTP for seven years, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the HV special police and the special police, as you refer to in that paragraph, are not part of the Croatian military?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I have learned today, I would have to agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You also, on the following paragraph, talk about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, could the witness please explain what he learned which led him to the conclusion he just gave. Because, Mr. Berikoff, in your -- one of your previous answers - and let me take you back to them - Mr. Kuzmanovic asked you the following: "When did you become aware that the special police of the Ministry of Interior was not a part of the Croatian military? What year?" So the question was about when. And then your answer was: "I never studied the Croatian forces in detail, so even to, right now, can I not answer that question probably accurately. My assessments are from dealing with both the Bosnian side and the Serb side. I had no dealings once I came to the OTP with the Croatian organisation chart." Now, that is a long answer, which does not directly deal with when you learned something. I understood, but, please, correct me when I'm wrong, I understood the answer to tell us that whether they were a part of the military organisation or not, that you had no good knowledge at the time to know and that has not really changed. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correctly understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Kuzmanovic, of course I had this question already on my mind but in relation to your last question from what the witness learned today, well, what the witness learned today has seen some documents which, as far as I can see, shed some light on some matters but not necessarily give a conclusive answer on some questions that might be on our mind. And apart from that, we learned from what the witness told us, so I would like to know what exactly you learned today, which now allows you to - and let me check the question again - what did you learn today which tell you that the HV special police and the special police, as you refer to in that paragraph, are not part of the Croatian military. So both HV special police and the special police, as you refer to, in the paragraph just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in looking at the various documents that I was shown this morning by Ms. Higgins, the address groups of the Ministry of Interior Major Ivan Juric or the special police was not present --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- in any of the documents. So based on that, I would have to agree that they were not in the chain of command, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's your conclusion and then for two HV special police and for other special police.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas in the beginning of your testimony you said that they were all the same to you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My initial assessment was, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that is the basis for agreeing with Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, do you know whether the Ministry of Interior special police -- I'll change the question. Do you know whether there were two sets of special police, one in the Ministry of Interior and one from the military police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware if there was or not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your statements, Mr. Berikoff, and we can go through them in detail if it's necessary, mention the special police in many different occasions, in many different locations as either conducting looting, manning check-points, or conducting burning. Now, is it fair to state that your -- you assumed that these were Ministry of Interior special police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume they were special police. I did not assume that they were part of the Ministry of Interior, sir. But I assume they were special police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And specifically in your supplemental statement you have -- in the paragraph below the one that we referred to previously. It says: "Mr. Berikoff stated that in his statements and exhibits he incorrectly attributed the burning and looting he witnessed in Kistanje on 9 August 1995 to both HV and special police on that day, he only saw the HV camouflaged soldiers going house to house, looting and burning in Kistanje. He attributed this to the special police as well, because when he met Ivan Juric outside of Kistanje on that day, Ivan Juric was wearing the grey uniform of the special police, and he believes that Ivan Juric was directing the activity in Kistanje." Now, a correct -- I mean, I read that statement, portion of your supplementary statement to mean that the special police was not involved in any way in Kistanje, correct, and the only reason you thought they were was because you assumed that Juric had something to do with the special police?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Berikoff, where the Ministry of Interior special police, where their battle sites were and from where and to where they went during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, in your supplemental statement you note in the paragraph below the one I just read, "... that the special police grey uniforms were not involved in the looting and burning he witnessed along the road from Knin to Drnis on 8 August 1995, as stated in his second statement at paragraph 2 (o). It was only the HV (camouflage) and the Croatian civilian police." So that's, Mr. Berikoff, a second area where you were that you mistakenly thought the Ministry of Interior special police were involved in looting and burning. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Once again it was an assumption on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And from the time that you gave your statements through and including -- up until the time that you give the supplemental statement in 2008, just a few days ago, on August 30th, what made you change your recollection? Was it Office of the Prosecutor speaking to you about this? Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't explain it. I think it was just -- it was not the Office of the Prosecutor that led me to this assessment. I think it was my own recollection of the number of incidents that happened and trying to remember everything. I could not recall with certainty whether it was special police, in my opinion, or not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it would be a guess?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Again, the following paragraph to the one that I just read: "Mr. Berikoff -- "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, what does that mean "so it's just a guess"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I can follow up on that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand the witness says I cannot say with certainty affirm what I earlier said was the case, which is not, in my view, a guess, but of course, you have to put some questions to the witness if on the basis of what the witness observed, what he observed, what he saw, as you rightly stated -- well, you -- we see that on the basis of what he observed, what he saw, that he could not reach certain conclusions he included in his earlier assessments. That is a fair statement of what he tells us. And in all your question -- in most of your questions you add something to that and you say for example, on the basis of your observations you could say that unit A, B, or C was involved because the way in which the witness has identified those units is -- is -- is not reliable. Uniforms, whatever. But then to say, Did you actually mean to say they were not involved requires a totally different kind of knowledge which is an oversight of everything. So let's try to focus on what the witness saw, what conclusions he earlier has drawn from those observations, and then to see to what extent these conclusions are corrected, are perhaps taken out, but not -- unless you specifically address the issue of whether he had a total overview, whether some units he may not have seen were involved or not in certain actions. You see my point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour, I will try to clear that up with my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, in your statements and in your supplemental statement specifically, you mention special police on many, many occasions. Is it fair to state that the sole factor for you to state that the special police were or were not involved in certain activities that you witnessed was based on the fact that they wore grey coverall-style uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, as well as a linking them with Major Juric who also wear grey coveralls and gave me the same assumption, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And we know now that Major Juric was not in any way with the Ministry of Interior special police. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I saw this morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So my statement is correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, the witness clearly says, he testified that he did not know who appointed Major Juric and that his charge where he puts him in a certain position is based on information which is apparently not very reliable. Now, whether he was involved in any way with that, it is a totally different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if the witness then says, On the basis of what I have seen he limits the source of his knowledge for the conclusion, and then to say, So you do agree with me, where you did not limit your question to that, is not what I expect to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, you also state in your supplemental statement the second-last paragraph on this particular page: "That the special police," and again you identify them in grey uniforms, "were not observing or directing traffic around the looting he witnessed between Knin and Drnis on 10 August. This was the Croatian civilian police." Now, again, your assumption that the special police were involved in directing traffic and/or involved in -- strike that. Your assumption is that it was the special police again because they wore grey uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me any facts that you have which would support the conclusion that the Ministry of Interior special police were involved in manning check-points?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us any facts to back up your conclusion in certain instances that you have not changed in your supplemental statement that demonstrate the Ministry of Interior special police were involved in looting?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Similarly can you give us any facts upon which you can base the conclusion that the Ministry of Interior special police were involved in burning?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please call up ERN -- we might have a D number for this, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, supplemental statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, Your Honour, I'd lake to move that supplemental statement, I'm sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I hear from the parties whether they consider supplemental statements to be 92 ter statements. These are written statements. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in a very strict sense I don't think we can consider them 92 ter statements unless the witness is taken through the formalities of the rule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is of course what I was hinting at, whether statements taken for the specific purposes of the proceedings before this Tribunal, whether we would need to meet the requirements of 92 ter. I don't want to be overformalistic on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But just for my information, how you consider this statement compared to the other statements which are 92 ter statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, from our perspective the statements are clearly written by the Prosecutor's office. They're not written in the first person as would a statement of the witness. Nevertheless, I do think the witness's review, acknowledgment on the actual document and again acknowledgment here in Court would suffice for us to have no problem with its admission to be included as consideration along with the 92 ter statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I would agree with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's, again, I just wanted to know from a procedural point of view what exactly the status is of the supplemental fact sheets. It's a kind of information on the basis of -- of the information given by the witness. Mr. Russo, I take it that I, because I see them now for the first time as well -- let me just check how they end. Yes, they are -- this is an -- this is a witness acknowledgment at the bottom of the supplemental sheet. Now, Mr. Berikoff, I make take it that what you -- the information you gave and which you confirmed in the witness acknowledgment under the supplemental information sheet that you gave this information to the best of your recollection, as being truthful, that if you were asked the same questions that you would have given the same questions -- same answers and that you would -- that you also acknowledge the accuracy of the way in which it was put on paper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number D735, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D735 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I know we've run into this issue before with the supplementals and I think probably that methodology of going through the 92 ter procedure should be done and I will remember that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we could do it if the witness is there and if the parties have no doubt as to whether this is really the -- the last information given by the witness even if it doesn't take the form of a statement in the proper sense. This is what I saw, et cetera --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- if you do that quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, what -- I mean the Prosecutor didn't move this document as part of its 92 ter submission obviously probably because of timing issues but there were substantial changes especially with regard to the special police so I would have thought they would have gone through that in direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, if these documents get the same status I think that would be appropriate, because it is a correction to or it is an addition to another 92 ter statement. Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, with regard to Mr. Kuzmanovic' last comment the Court can check the transcript, I did go through all of the corrections which are contained on the supplemental information sheet with the witness prior to submitting his statements as 92 ter. He made the corrections, he made the clarifications which are contained in that document and that's the procedure by which the OTP has chosen to deal with the supplemental information sheets. We certainly have no problem with them being admitted along with that. I just believe it is a difference of procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Russo, of course the Chamber is lost under those circumstances. Why, because you go through some corrections, but we haven't seen the supplemental information sheet. Therefore, we cannot see whether everything which is contained in the supplemental information sheet has been covered by you. So, it may well be true what you say, but at the time you are doing it we cannot verify whether that's the case yes or no. Now, if, of course, you have gone through all the details of everything that was corrected or what was added, then of course there would be no need for Mr. Kuzmanovic to, again, get this admitted into evidence, because then it is already part of your examination-in-chief. I can't verify it now. I would have to read the supplemental information sheet in full detail in order to know whether everything has been covered in your examination-in-chief. Let's not spend too much time on it. It certainly doesn't hurt if, in addition to the examination-in-chief the supplemental information sheet is now admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, I will call 3D00-1871, please. Mr. Berikoff, this was an article written by Garth Pritchard that you had provided to the Office of the Prosecutor and they had provided to the Defence and which you brought with you to your proofing session?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Pritchard was someone you spoke to at the time of the events in Knin, after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the article, in the first page, toward the bottom, says, talking about Knin and I'll read from the line that says: "This time." "This time Knin is back in the Croatian fold, so to speak, but is a devastated, ravaged, broken town scene of massive looting, reprisals killing not by the triumphant Croatian blitzkrieg that recaptured the whole of Krajina in early August but by those who followed the disciplined, controlled Croatian army." Were you the source of information for the section in this article that discusses the controlled -- disciplined controlled Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Then on the second page of this particular article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could go to the top of the second page, please. Actually, the bottom of this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You had made a correction in your supplemental statement at the bottom of the page. There's a discussion that begins: "Then there's captain Phil Berikoff of the Vandoos." You were not a member of the Vandoos, correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it discusses the things that you had done, including, at the bottom, he, meaning Berikoff, tells of finding a woman on a corner just after the Croatian army swept through. If we could scroll to the top of the page because that is where I had read to and if we could move the document to the left. Not all of it had been included in the scan but most of it has. "She was hysterical and wailing and surrounded by her family, husband and eight children all dead. I tried to persuade her to come to the camp but she wouldn't leave her familiar. He finally got body-bags, put the dead in them and had them pulled off to the side of the road to be picked up later. The woman still wouldn't leave. When Berikoff returned the next day, the woman was gone and tire tracks of trucks led off the road and over the body-bags which had been ripped open and bodies mutilated, just another day in the Balkans." Now, Mr. Berikoff, that's really not what happened, was it?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not at all what happened, sir, and that is why I brought the article to the proofing session because it is totally erroneous information. The facts are not accurate in that paragraph at all, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you deny telling Mr. Pritchard this particular story?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the story about the mortar shell that hit the intersection nor about the woman wailing as she sat beside her husband. There were in fact no children involved at all. The number eight is definitely is wrong. The track trucks, et cetera, over the body-bags is also wrong. There was only the one body-bag that was -- to the best of my recollection that was run over by a tank and riddled with bullets. So the whole paragraph is filled with erroneous information, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any idea where Mr. Pritchard got that erroneous information?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was not from you?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from me. Bits and pieces were. I took him out to the intersection. However, I did not give those figures at all, because they are not accurate in the least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that this article, at least parts of this article and the part I reflected on where we discussed it was incorrect information that was spread out to the world about what happened during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, and that's why I brought the article to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes exhibit number D736.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we decide on admission --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- What is the probative value apart from that nothing is right in this article?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think it goes to describe that Mr. Berikoff is purported to be quoted in this article or the information is purported to be given from him in this article and I'm demonstrating that based on information that was erroneous, many things in this article are incorrect just like the assumption that the special police were involved in various areas has been incorrect, just like the fact that there were eight children dead, which is incorrect. You know, just an example of how information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: -- gets twisted and distorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I hope, Mr. Kuzmanovic, that this Chamber will not have to look at all the incorrect information about what happened even it is an attributed to a witness that takes distance of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour. Just an example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And therefore the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber admits the document into evidence, and just to avoid whatever confusion, it is D736. What I said, you'll understand is of some guidance. We have still some pending issues about publications being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One could even think of it as a notorious fact that a lot of wrong information is published especially about war circumstances. Again, it is admitted and the Chamber accepts your explanation. At the same time, as guidance for the parties, let's try not to include in the evidence everything that was written by whomever at whatever time on whatever information, because the trial might take another six months. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour. It was simply an example, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, the Ministry of Interior special police -- and you had said earlier the Prosecutor did not bring to your attention where they were and what kind of activities they were involved in. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- not that I recall, sir, no, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware aside from the Office of the Prosecutor that the Ministry of Interior special police were involved in front line military activities?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that when you were in Donji Lapac that the Ministry of Interior special police were already out of Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we could just have a clarification on that, I think the witness's evidence is that he was in Donji Lapac on two separate days. If that questions includes both days, I believe it is the 11th and 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And that question does include both days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that on 11th and 12th August of 1995 the Ministry of Interior special police were already out of Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. I did not know that the Ministry of Interior was involved. I assumed -- my assumption was because of the mixture of grey coveralls and camouflage uniforms, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So your sole basis for determining that the Ministry of Interior special police were in Donji Lapac when you were there at the same time? on the 11th and 12th of August of 1995 was the grey coveralls?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my assessment throughout the whole sector, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the significance of the battle that went on in Donji Lapac, in terms of artillery?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't, sir. I know there was heavier than usual fighting up in the Donji Lapac area, but I was not aware of the significance at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that when ... thank you, Your Honour. Were you aware that when the Ministry of Interior special police took Donji Lapac that they came under friendly fire, artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that, but as I say, I knew there was heavier than usual fighting in the Donji Lapac area, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe or hear that the ARSK forces shelled Donji Lapac after the Ministry of Interior special police had taken the town?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but once again I will go back to my answer that there was fighting, so it is logical that there would have been a return of fire, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please call up P614. And page 23, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, I'll represent to that you this is a Prosecution tendered document dated November 26th, 2001, to the Chief of Staff of the Croatian army, entitled Analysis of the progress of Operation Storm. Page 23 of this document discusses the progress of day 4 of Operation Storm and specifically mentions the special police of the Ministry of Interior. If you go to page 25 of this document, please, there's a notation at 1400 hours on the 7th of August of 1995 that Donji Lapac is liberated. And below that, that Donji Lapac suffered friendly fire artillery with no casualties. Now, if we go to page 31 -- actually, page 30, I'm sorry. This is progress of day 6 of Operation Storm, 9 August 1995. Do you know where the city or village of Kulen Vakuf was in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not offhand, no I do not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you up among the Bosnian border near Donji Lapac?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Donji Lapac, and then I was taken to one crossing point. I don't recall exactly where the crossing point is, sir. The Jordanian I believe it was the Deputy Commander or the Chief of Staff took me to the border crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at page 31 of this report, again on the 9th of August, at 1900 hours, it shows that the special police staff in Ostrovica village ceased work and the special police forces that had been engaged there were sent to their home units with the approval of the operation commander. Now, you said earlier you were not aware that the Ministry of Interior special police had been called to stand down as of August 9th to go back to their home units. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of what units or troops were in Donji Lapac when you were there on the 11th and 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. The reason I went up to Donji Lapac was to follow the alleged route of the evacuation of civilians and the withdrawal of the ARSK up towards the Donji Lapac area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It's fair to state that you cannot state with any certainty whether the Ministry of Interior --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour, and I apologise again to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: It is fair to state, Mr. Berikoff, that you cannot state with any certainty whether the Ministry of Interior special police were involved in any way in the burning and/or looting of Donji Lapac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a fair statement, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Could I please call D557.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berikoff, D557 is an order from the Chief of Staff of the Croatian army, Mr. Cervenko, ordering the Ministry of Interior special police to take up positions in the area of Petrova Gora. Do you know where the area of Petrova Gora is?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall where the area is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Is it in Sector North?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in the northern portion, from what I believe. I don't know if it is actually in Sector North or not but it is in the northern portion, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So at least this particular order, D557 shows that the Ministry of Interior special police were in the -- ordered to go the area of Petrova Gora as of 10th of August 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the information shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't have any information to the contrary. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROY BERIKOFF [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in order to save time there are several other documents that I would like to refer to that have been marked in evidence both by the Prosecution and the Defence, I can speak with Mr. Russo about them during the break, that show when and where the Ministry of Interior special police were in this time-frame and that they were not areas of Kistanje, Civljane, Drnis, and other places where Mr. Berikoff states that he thought he saw Ministry of Interior special police conducting burning and/or looting. So I can speak with Mr. Russo about that rather than having to go through each of the documents with Mr. Berikoff, for reference purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can imagine that you put to the witness that there are documents which say that the special police were at place A where the witness said they were at place B. However, the evaluation of that information, whether the document is wrong, whether the recollection of the witness is wrong, whether there were several units at several places is of course all a matter of evaluation of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there is no problem in putting this to the witness, but seeking from this witness, who may have limited oversight over the totality of the information, seeking him to draw conclusions is tasking him to some extent with what is the task of this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, the Chamber, despite perhaps the wisdom and knowledge of Mr. Berikoff would take that task as its own task.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Understood. And that was my whole purpose in asking that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would keep that in the back of your mind and if perhaps you, together with Mr. Russo, try to summarize the gist of those documents so that you can put it to the witness, we have documents that say, there, there, et cetera, then you can put that to the witness you can put that to the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and get his response.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: We can do that -- I see it's break time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's break time. Mr. Berikoff, we will have a break for 25 minutes. Could you give us an indication, Mr. Kuzmanovic, on how much more?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask how much time I have used so far. I thought I said an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to rely on Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Putting him under the gun here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Net time was a little bit over half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I -- I would like to -- I'm probably going to use the rest of my hour, Your Honour. I said an hour and a half. I might be done in less than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. All right. We will have a break and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any report on the matter I raised earlier today, about translations. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning Mr. President, Your Honours. Yes, according to our count there are 251 exhibits that are still labelled draft or unrevised but that is a continuous process so I think we are, over time receiving the final translations and hopefully within, I guess, a couple of months we'll down to zero.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there at least we have provision translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other report. Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We just sent a report to the registry and it is about 19 exhibits that we are still waiting for appropriate translations, and we will check out whether this will be due in a due time and then we could inform the Chamber more precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can report that the Gotovina Defence does not have any outstanding translation issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you didn't miss the deadline.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then one other issue, P760 was MFI'd for the time being. The Chamber said that it would consider admission. The Chamber has decided that P760 will not be admitted into evidence. There are various reasons for that, one of them being that if the author is unknown that this is a risk that this document, which is not very clear as to the facts on which it is based, but there is even a risk that it repeats evidence, which has been given already by witnesses before this Court, because if you do not know who the author is, and certainly this document has not been put to all of the witnesses, it's too -- the Chamber considers that the probative value of it is subject to such serious doubts and risks that it should not be admitted into evidence. And I think it is important for the parties to know before that witness leaves this courtroom. Mr. Kuzmanovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will -- Your Honour should know that Mr. Russo and I did discuss the issue of Ministry of Interior special police documents that show the locations of which -- where the special police were during the time-frame of Operation Storm and we've come to the agreement it's not the exclusive list of where they were but for the purpose of these dates, we've agreed to those exhibit numbers, and when I find my list, Your Honour, I will make sure I read them. Mr. Russo can correct me if I'm wrong. Am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: He's not wrong, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
